title: refactor(ci): split lint/test/release workflows and optimize cache parallelism
author: Aisha Khan
description: Motivation: our monolithic CI workflow has grown slow and brittle; lint, unit tests, and release automation run in a single matrix which increases queue time and cache contention. This PR splits lint/test/release into separate workflows, consolidates reusable workflow_step files, upgrades a few actions to their latest major versions, and adjusts cache keys and parallelism heuristics to reduce cache misses and speed up job startup. Summary of changes: 1) Introduced .github/workflows/lint.yml, test.yml, release.yml. 2) Extracted shared steps to .github/workflows/ci-steps/*.yml (checkout, setup-node, restore-cache, setup-go) to reduce duplication. 3) Updated actions/setup-node from v3 to v4 and actions/cache bump to v4. 4) Adjusted cache key templates to include matrix.os and node-version and added a short-fingerprint based on lockfile to avoid stale caches across minor installs. 5) Reduced overly aggressive matrix permutations (removed redundant Node/OS combos for lint) and introduced a lightweight fast-lint job for pushes to branches to improve quick feedback. 6) Tuned job concurrency and parallelism: increased restore timeout, enabled cache-level concurrency, and split largest integration tests into two parallel shards. Checklist: - [x] Split workflows and verify logic locally - [x] CI runs green on fork + branch - [x] Confirmed action compatibility with Node 20 and Linux/arm runners - [x] Coordinated with release-engineering for release.yml changes How tested: ran the new workflows on the feature branch and on a temporary fork; observed ~25% reduction in median queue-to-first-step time and ~18% reduction in total wall time for PR runs for typical changes. Release automation was exercised in a dry-run (no release published) to validate tagging, changelog generation, and upload steps. Related Linear: ENG-1423. Notes: this refactor aims for hygiene and developer experience improvements only; no product-facing behavior changes. If problems appear we can revert the top-level workflow and re-enable the consolidated workflow. Links: internal CI run: https://ci.redwood.internal/runs/348492 (private), proposal doc: https://linear.app/redwood/issue/ENG-1423/ci-split-and-cache-optimizations
release_notes: Split CI workflows for faster incremental runs; reduced cache contention and improved parallelism; internal-only infra changes; no user-facing changes.
commits: feat(ci): add lint.yml and extract shared ci steps
chore(ci): update actions/setup-node to v4 and actions/cache to v4
perf(ci): tune cache keys and parallelism for integration test shards
docs(ci): add comments/explainers for cache key choices
comments: Diego Rivera: Overall looks good. Two requests: 1) can we avoid including node-version in the lint cache to increase reuse across minor bumps? 2) please add a short blurb to ci/README.md describing when to add a new matrix axis.
Aisha Khan: Thanks Diego — good call. Adjusted lint cache key to omit node-version for the fast-lint job and added the README blurb. Also added a test flag to opt into node-matrix for full-test runs.
Priya Desai: Verified release dry-run on staging; changelog generation step had a transient timeout which we mitigated by increasing the HTTP timeout and adding retry. Approving after that fix.
Ben Thompson: Left a small nit on variable naming in ci-steps/setup-node.yml but not blocking. Approving.
CI Bot: lint (node) — passed, unit tests (go/python) — passed, integration (sharded) — passed, release dry-run — passed
ci_checks_summary: lint: pass (fast-lint on pushes, full-lint on PRs), unit: pass (go & python), integration: pass (2 shards), release: dry-run pass. One transient timeout fixed and rerun.
notes_for_ops: Release workflow modifies tagging and changelog steps; release engineering reviewed and signed off. If any downstream jobs rely on the old consolidated workflow name, update references to .github/workflows/release.yml.
